_pilot: EXPANDED pilot corpus. Byte targets are 2.25x the token-derived targets.
Measured 2026-08-09: prepare_brittain3.py keeps ONE ~1000-token window per
document and discards the rest, so only 49.2% of collected tokens ever reach
training. At 1x the schedule would have been 2.21 epochs over 320M usable
tokens, contradicting the brief's '708M mostly unique tokens'.
Per-category keep rates measured: code 48%, documentation 45%, english 63%,
structured 32%, exercises 100% (their documents are already short).
The exercises slice is generated separately and is NOT scaled here: its
ceiling is template diversity, not bytes. See docs/BRITTAIN3_PILOT.md.
_code_language_shares: Python/TypeScript/JavaScript are from the brief. The remaining 20% split
across go/rust/java_kotlin/c_cpp/shell is a proposal, not a specified value.
Key names must match normalize_language() buckets: 'java_kotlin', not 'java'.
There is deliberately no 'other' key, so any language outside this list gets
a zero quota and is rejected.
_repository_cap: 4MB, down from 20MB for the tokenizer corpus. This corpus is a third the
size, so the old cap would let one large repository own a visible slice.
